approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Both mutation sources and crossover partners are drawn from preferred score bands, with uniform choice inside each band and exclusion of the first parent when choosing its partner. A fingerprint Gaussian process trained on every accepted label then selects which generated offspring are evaluated. The implementation already favors strong individual parents, but it does not use molecular similarity when deciding which two parents to recombine.
approach.novelty: Condition the crossover partner choice on similarity to the already selected first parent, using the same fingerprint definition that the Parent already declares. More similar eligible partners receive more of the chosen score band's probability, while the first-parent rule and score-band preference remain intact. This tests whether recombining related high-scoring molecules preserves useful local structure more often. The completed siblings altered core balance and survivor diversity; this experiment changes compatibility of a parent pair without replacing survivors or changing crossover chemistry.

hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.

finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.
finding_summary.results: The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyl and amine families carry reactive halogens, strained connections and repeated large assemblies
molecular.overall_character: All current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is predominantly aromatic and ring-bearing: aromatic-token rates range from 0.9701 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9805 to 0.9908. Compact fused heteroaromatic amides, aryl-linked saturated amines and quinoline/pyrrole/lactam combinations coexist with very large repeated dione, ester and carbonate assemblies. The most size-expanded task has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253, while tiny fragments also occur throughout the trajectories. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. This leaves potentially basic nitrogen centres drawn without a solution ionization state and stereogenic bridged or substituted rings without configurations. Diversity is moderate across seed families but often narrow within a leading series. Familiar medicinal fragments are present, yet overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because N-halogen and acyl-halide groups, N-N and N-O connections, strained small rings, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact fused and bridged aza-aromatic systems with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. Alkyl and ether substitution decorate the ring framework; several leading amides are directly N-fluorinated. A related family contains a conventional N-H amide and a thiophenol substituent, while another has an ordinary sulfur bridge and aryl ketone. Other seeds produce N-chloro amides or cumulated unsaturation in larger heterocycles. The lowest proposals are tiny imine or halogen-containing fragments, and a late elaborated amide product adds another ring/carbonyl connection with a much lower score. Conventional carbonyl fragments are recognizable, but the bridged topology and reactive nitrogen substituents limit synthetic confidence.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are reactive functionality rather than ordinary aryl halogenation.
Some relatives add thiols, O-Br groups or unusual unsaturation, including a cumulated-double-bond string rate of 0.0816.
Bridged ring arrangements and appended carbonyl rings increase geometric and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and over-elaborated products lose the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.

Matched stable nitrogen substituents and ordinary ring connections around the leading framework are incomplete; the N-H amide and conventional sulfide/ketone relatives already show viable alternative chemistry.
Configurations at substituted bridge atoms are unspecified, and cumulated unsaturation in other relatives lacks a demonstrated feasible geometry.

Replacing a ring methyl by methylthio gives 0.4166419114047398 for the same halogen pair, so sulfur addition is not rewarded in that local comparison. A conventional N-H amide relative reaches 0.4254027310763201 and an aryl ketone/sulfide relative reaches 0.42570769607214154; N-fluorination is therefore not universal among the stronger outputs. The more elaborated final amide structure scores 0.015332630870835013, and tiny fragments score 0.0. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.4163503402962837 and 0.40143692941489145 versus parental 0.4463521672202675 and 0.4126819838532174. per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains N-methylated heteroaromatic diones, substituted aza-aromatic ester groups and imine-containing unsaturated side chains with oxygen-linked alkynes. Some members join multiple copies of these motifs through branched carbon or ether-containing connections. Additional variants contain a chlorinated oxime ether connection, cyanate-like substitution or direct N-chlorination. Seed 0 produces very large multiaryl ester/carbonate assemblies with several nitriles; seed 1 develops fused carbonyl-rich heterocycles. The low tail includes simple hydrocarbons and an extremely strained small cyclic alkyne. The output has abundant polar and aromatic fragments, but repeated growth and reactive appendages dominate practical synthesis concerns.
liabilities: Oxygen-linked alkynes, imines, chlorinated oxime ethers, direct N-Cl and O-Cl variants introduce reactive chemistry.
Repeated dione/aryl/ester units and many ester or carbonate connections add size, flexibility and hydrolysis-sensitive bonds.
The small cyclic alkyne in the low tail is a particularly clear example of graph validity not establishing a plausible molecular geometry.
missing_features: Small isolated fragments lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl arrangement of the stronger products.
The leading set incompletely represents stable, less repetitive structures that retain the useful core; the smaller example already has a score close to much larger relatives.
Imine/alkene geometry and configurations of branched linkers are unassigned, while some small-ring alternatives require extreme geometric distortion.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

applicability_conditions: This experiment changes the parent-allocation service in the active feedback_memory Layer. The first parent and score-band preference remain inherited, and all partners are accepted current survivors with real same-objective labels.

The declared conditional effect requires an eligible partner band with unequal fingerprint similarities to the actual first parent. The Parent supplies 33542 such opportunities, 769 singleton states, one other equal-similarity state and no all-zero state; unobserved branches remain explicitly bounded.

The fingerprint definition is reused as fixed allocation metadata and the Gaussian process itself is unchanged. Fingerprint similarity does not identify matching physical attachment sites, stereochemical compatibility, synthetic accessibility, stability or common pharmacology.

Partner weighting can intensify inbreeding and narrow reachable cores or increase duplicate/invalid graph attempts. More similar parents are a compatibility hypothesis, not an assurance that the unchanged random fragment operator preserves useful groups.

A zero-similarity member receives no conditional mass when positive-similarity alternatives exist, but an all-zero or all-equal band uses inherited uniform sampling. The mechanism adds no chemical rejection filter and makes no score claim for omitted pairings.

The weaker historical crossover yield has confounded parent thresholds and selected proposal distributions. Paired complete evaluations are needed to assess transfer; same-state similarity enrichment establishes allocation only, and shared two-parent outcomes do not identify an individual causal parent's contribution.

research_intent.falsifier: The assortative allocation mechanism is refuted if it uses a molecule outside the accepted contemporaneous population, mismatches the first-parent identity, violates the original score-band/exclusion rule, computes fingerprints with changed representation settings, or selects informative partners contrary to the declared similarity/normalization/inverse-CDF law. Complete nondegenerate evidence with unequal partner similarities but no conditional-probability displacement or changed pairing fails the intended activation. If every partner opportunity is singleton or equal-similarity, activation is inconclusive rather than demonstrated; missing pairing diagnostics likewise makes it inconclusive. Correctly increased conditional similarity and changed pairings with worse valid yield, fewer parent/incumbent beats or lower final scores is negative compatibility-transfer evidence, not retrospective nonexecution. Changing the first-parent sampling rule, survivor selection, graph operators, posterior model or within-pool acquisition outside this pairing mechanism violates the component scope.
research_intent.implementation_change: Edit only worktree optimize.py inside feedback_memory. Preserve the complete accepted archive, score/serial-greedy bounded survivor population, admission and pending provenance, original molecular identities and Individual/parent-record interfaces. Add a task-local cache of binary Morgan fingerprints for accepted survivor molecules solely as parent-pair allocation metadata. Construct its RDKit generator from the Parent's unchanged posterior_selector fingerprint_radius, fingerprint_bits and include_chirality settings; do not modify, invoke or populate the posterior's own learned/feature state. No representation parameter is added or tuned. Preserve the complete existing score-band construction, band weights, excluded-partner handling and band draw. For a first-parent call with no excluded identity, retain the exact inherited uniform rng.choice operation and do not condition it on chemistry. For a partner call, resolve the excluded identity to the actual first parent in the current scored population. On the already chosen post-exclusion eligible band, compute each candidate partner's binary-fingerprint Tanimoto similarity s_i to that first parent, and draw with probability s_i/sum(s). This is stochastic assortative mating, not nearest-neighbor determinism or an added novelty filter. If all similarities are equal, including an all-zero vector, preserve the exact inherited uniform choice; a legacy call whose excluded identity cannot be resolved also preserves uniform choice with an explicit diagnostic. finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.

finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.
finding_summary.results: The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyl and amine families carry reactive halogens, strained connections and repeated large assemblies
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is predominantly aromatic and ring-bearing: aromatic-token rates range from 0.9701 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9805 to 0.9908. Compact fused heteroaromatic amides, aryl-linked saturated amines and quinoline/pyrrole/lactam combinations coexist with very large repeated dione, ester and carbonate assemblies. The most size-expanded task has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253, while tiny fragments also occur throughout the trajectories. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. This leaves potentially basic nitrogen centres drawn without a solution ionization state and stereogenic bridged or substituted rings without configurations. Diversity is moderate across seed families but often narrow within a leading series. Familiar medicinal fragments are present, yet overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because N-halogen and acyl-halide groups, N-N and N-O connections, strained small rings, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact fused and bridged aza-aromatic systems with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. Alkyl and ether substitution decorate the ring framework; several leading amides are directly N-fluorinated. A related family contains a conventional N-H amide and a thiophenol substituent, while another has an ordinary sulfur bridge and aryl ketone. Other seeds produce N-chloro amides or cumulated unsaturation in larger heterocycles. The lowest proposals are tiny imine or halogen-containing fragments, and a late elaborated amide product adds another ring/carbonyl connection with a much lower score. Conventional carbonyl fragments are recognizable, but the bridged topology and reactive nitrogen substituents limit synthetic confidence.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are reactive functionality rather than ordinary aryl halogenation.
Some relatives add thiols, O-Br groups or unusual unsaturation, including a cumulated-double-bond string rate of 0.0816.
Bridged ring arrangements and appended carbonyl rings increase geometric and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and over-elaborated products lose the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.

Matched stable nitrogen substituents and ordinary ring connections around the leading framework are incomplete; the N-H amide and conventional sulfide/ketone relatives already show viable alternative chemistry.
Configurations at substituted bridge atoms are unspecified, and cumulated unsaturation in other relatives lacks a demonstrated feasible geometry.

Replacing a ring methyl by methylthio gives 0.4166419114047398 for the same halogen pair, so sulfur addition is not rewarded in that local comparison. A conventional N-H amide relative reaches 0.4254027310763201 and an aryl ketone/sulfide relative reaches 0.42570769607214154; N-fluorination is therefore not universal among the stronger outputs. The more elaborated final amide structure scores 0.015332630870835013, and tiny fragments score 0.0. These observations favor a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement without isolating one universally required heteroatom bond.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains N-methylated heteroaromatic diones, substituted aza-aromatic ester groups and imine-containing unsaturated side chains with oxygen-linked alkynes. Some members join multiple copies of these motifs through branched carbon or ether-containing connections. approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Both mutation sources and crossover partners are drawn from preferred score bands, with uniform choice inside each band and exclusion of the first parent when choosing its partner. A fingerprint Gaussian process trained on every accepted label then selects which generated offspring are evaluated. The implementation already favors strong individual parents, but it does not use molecular similarity when deciding which two parents to recombine.
approach.novelty: Condition the crossover partner choice on similarity to the already selected first parent, using the same fingerprint definition that the Parent already declares. More similar eligible partners receive more of the chosen score band's probability, while the first-parent rule and score-band preference remain intact. This tests whether recombining related high-scoring molecules preserves useful local structure more often. The completed siblings altered core balance and survivor diversity; this experiment changes compatibility of a parent pair without replacing survivors or changing crossover chemistry.
